meta.title: Ch 13: Group Audits — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 13 (Group Audits).

questions.q: The group engagement partner's responsibility for the group audit opinion:
o: Is diluted where components are audited by other firms
Is not reduced by reliance on component auditors' work — the partner alone signs the group opinion
Delegates final review to the component auditors
Is satisfied by receiving signed reports
questions.why: SA 600: the group auditor is solely responsible for the opinion; component auditors' work is directed, reviewed and (where needed) re-performed — 'I relied on them' is not a defence; materiality allocation and involvement are the levers.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the opinion's weight is not shareable — nor is the blame Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

questions.q: Materiality for a component (when the group auditor sets it) is:
o: Equal to group materiality
Lower than group performance/overall materiality, sized so that a component's uncorrected + undetected misstatements, aggregated group-wide, stay under group thresholds
10% of the component's assets
Decided by the component auditor alone
questions.why: Component materiality is set by the group engagement team; must be lower than group materiality to cover aggregation risk; components can be 'significant' by size or risk characteristics (e.g. specific transactions that matter to the group).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — a slice's budget must protect the whole pie AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: When the group team receives a component auditor's findings on a significant risk, it should:
o: Attach the component report to the file untouched
Evaluate, request additional work where needed, and assess implications for group risk assessment and the report
Rely as a legal opinion
Ignore where the component is immaterial in size
questions.why: Communication is two-way and includes the group's inquiries on independence, the component's identified risks/misstatements/exceptions; the group team EVALUATES — that is the verb the standards use; a small component can hold a big risk.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — 'component is small' is about size, not significance-by-nature AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Two-way communication with component auditors
mem.tip: A quiet room can house the loudest pipe.

questions.q: Component materiality compared with group materiality is:
o: Higher
Lower
Equal
Half of PM
questions.why: Set lower by the group team to keep the aggregate of component undetected/unfound errors under the group threshold.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the slice's cap is below the pie's AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Divide the budget, double the caution.

questions.q: Who is responsible for the group audit opinion?
o: Every component auditor
The group engagement partner/team — sole, not diluted
The audit committee
The exchange
questions.why: Reliance transfers work, not responsibility; the group team directs and reviews.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the signature doesn't share the blame AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: One report, one signature, no co-authors.

questions.q: Under the revised group-audit standards, the group engagement team's rights over component auditors include:
o: No rights beyond the report
Direction (component materiality, required work), timely TWO-WAY communication, and access to / involvement with their documentation as the risk warrants
Only re-performing all their work
Outsourcing the report to them
questions.why: The revision tightened the group team's control over the component auditor's work (and access to documentation) — the exam point: reliance is active, supervised, and evidenced, not postal.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — direction, involvement, review — the verbs AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Group audit — component auditor access
mem.tip: A group audit is conducted, not collected.

questions.q: Before directing component auditors, the group team must establish:
o: The fee split
The consolidation scope (which components are included and on what basis) — the boundary error (omitted entity) is a group-level misstatement risk
The language
Local tax filings
questions.why: Group audits fail at the boundary: an unconsolidated special-purpose vehicle or a post-year disposal treated wrongly poisons the consolidated numbers whatever the components audit says — the scoping memo is the first review.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — consolidation errors are group-material by construction AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Get the perimeter wrong and the sum of right parts is wrong.

questions.q: A group team cannot obtain sufficient evidence over a non-significant but pervasive segment. The correct report:
o: Is always unmodified
The limitation applies to the GROUP audit: qualified or disclaimed depending on materiality/pervasiveness of the unavailable segment's possible effects
Mentions the component auditor's fee
Is delayed by one year
questions.why: Component materiality and significance don't set the report ceiling — the effect at GROUP level does; a small but decisive line (a key subsidiary's cash, unconfirmed) can push the group to a disclaimer.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — significance at component, consequence at group Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A missing piece is judged by the picture, not its size.

questions.q: Group overall materiality Rs 1,200 lakh; the engagement team sets a component's materiality at 60%. The correct framing of the resulting Rs 720 lakh is:
o: Component materiality Rs 720 lakh (60% of group OM) — must be below group OM; and group PM governs the total
Equal to group OM of Rs 1,200 lakh
Larger for a 'significant' component so it gets less work
Set independently by the component auditor with no group input
questions.why: Component materiality must be lower than group materiality — the sum of undetected component errors should remain below group thresholds; it is set by the GROUP engagement team (option 4 is wrong), and significant status doesn't raise it (more scrutiny, lower floor).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — allocation logic beats allocation numbers in group-audit questions AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Component materiality < group overall; aggregation risk is why; a component's uncorrected errors must stay small enough to be safe in total.
